newsitem.title: INDIA: India gold, silver close lower on dull world trend.
newsitem.headline: India gold, silver close lower on dull world trend.

text.p: ** Standard gold 24 carats closes 15 rupees lower at 4,780 rupees per 10 grammes on a dull world trend and poor demand. It lost 10 rupees on Thursday.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) close steady at 56,000 rupees per piece, 200 rupees lower than the previous close. Gold biscuits lost 100 rupees to 56,200 rupees per piece on Thursday.
** Silver (.999) close 15 rupees lower at 6,840 rupees per kg on dull world trend and improved arrivals. Silver lost 55 rupees to 6,855 rupees per kg on Thursday.
Standard gold 24 carats fell 15 rupees to 4,780 rupees per 10 grammes on dull demand and in line with falling prices in world markets. Gold fell 10 rupees to 4,795 per 10 grammes on Thursday.
"It's psychological. People are waiting for a further fall in prices," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani. "They may wait for a week and not beyong that."
Damani said arrivals of imported gold too improved, creating a situation of surplus.
Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) closed 200 rupees lower at 56,000 rupees per piece. They lost 100 rupees to 56,200 rupees on Thursday.
Silver .999 fell by 15 rupees to 6,840 rupees per kg on heavy arrivals and poor demand. Silver lost 55 rupees to 6,855 rupees per kg on Thursday.
"The market will mainly depend on world trends to find its tone. It should perk up on marriage season demand," Damani said. (Conversion $1=35.76 rupees)
